result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more processes touching the same resource. With a shared log, two scripts writing at once can interleave their output mid-line or mid-block.

To avoid it, open the log in append mode and take an exclusive lock with `flock` around each write:

```sh
(
  flock 9
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >&9
) 9>>"$LOG"
```

The lock is released when the subshell exits, so a crashed writer cannot leave it held.

`flock` is advisory, so it only protects you if every script that writes to the log uses it.

A single short `echo ... >> "$LOG"` is usually safe without a lock on a local filesystem, because each append is one atomic write. The lock matters once an entry spans several commands or lines.

On NFS neither guarantee is reliable; there, send entries through a single writer such as `logger`/syslog instead.
